title: Why you see things that are not there
hook: Why do you sometimes see things that are not actually there?

narration.text: Your brain sometimes creates what it expects to see, even if it is not real.
This is called top-down processing, where expectations shape perception.
It means your brain uses prior knowledge and context to interpret sensory input.
So, if you expect a familiar face in a crowd, you might briefly "see" it.
This helps us quickly make sense of the world, filling in missing details.
However, it can also lead to illusions or misinterpretations of reality.
Our brains are constantly predicting, rather than just passively observing.
Have you ever experienced seeing something that was not truly there?

description: Discover the fascinating reason your brain sometimes shows you things that are not actually present. Learn about top-down processing and how your expectations can influence what you perceive in the world around you.
topic: Why you sometimes see things that are not there when your mind expects them, explaining top-down processing in perception.
